practiceProblems.title: Simple Bank Transfer System
practiceProblems.description:
The **Simple Bank Transfer System** is a lightweight, secure web application that simulates one of the most essential banking functions: **direct, real-time money transfers between users**. With a clean, user-friendly interface and robust backend architecture, it allows customers to manage their funds seamlessly while giving administrators full visibility into transaction activities.
For this project the Frontend part is already given to you so the main focus should be on building the backend.

#### Tech Stack

**Backend Application Architecture**
* **Backend**: Secure RESTful APIs with user authentication & role-based access control
* **Database**: Persistent data storage and transaction logging
* **Authentication**: Token-based (e.g., JWT) for secure sessions


#### Key Features

The application provides two distinct experiences:

#### Customer Dashboard

* **Secure Registration & Login**
 * Users can register with their name, email, and password.
 * Every new account is initialized with a **₹10,000** balance.
 * Secure token-based login system ensures protected user sessions.

* **Real-Time Money Transfer**
 * View current balance upon login
 * Transfer money to any other registered user via a dynamic dropdown
 * Transfers are validated and processed **instantly**
 * Prevents overdrafts: users cannot send more than their balance


#### Admin Dashboard

* **Role-Based Access**

 * Only users with the `Admin` role can access this section

* **Complete Transaction Log**
 * View all transaction history in **reverse chronological order**
 * Each entry includes:
 * Sender Name
 * Recipient Name
 * Amount Transferred
 * Date & Time

* **Read-Only & Auditable**

 * Ensures separation of duties and tamper-proof oversight


#### How It Works: User Flow

1. **Onboarding**
 * Register 3 users: one Admin, two Customers (e.g., Customer A & B)

2. **Customer Action**
 * Customer A logs in → sees balance: ₹10,000
 * Selects Customer B → Enters ₹500 → Clicks "Send Money"
 * System processes transfer → Customer A’s new balance: ₹9,500
 * Customer B’s balance: ₹10,500

3. **Admin Oversight**
 * Admin logs in → Sees a new log entry:

 ```
 Customer A sent ₹500 to Customer B 
 On: [Date and Time]
 ```


#### Highlights
* Secure user sessions with role-based routing
* Smooth multi-step money transfer logic
* Fully auditable transaction history
* Practical full-stack example of real-time state change


#### Ideal For:
* Full-stack development practice
* Demonstrating secure and responsive web applications
* Learning how to implement financial logic and audit systems

practiceProblems.title: User database and server setup
practiceProblems.description:
Now we are going to build our application from scratch

First of all we need to establish our backend server for which we are going to use express, mongoose, and dotenv. And we will setup our database for the users too here.

### Task:
1. Write your own mongo connection string in .env file. 
2. Write the user database schema to include all these: 

| Field | Type | Required | Unique | Default | Enum | Description |
|-----------|--------|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|-------------------|
| name | String | No | No | None | N/A | User's name |
| email | String | Yes | Yes | None | N/A | User's email |
| password | String | Yes | No | None | N/A | User's password |
| role | String | No | No | "customer"| "customer", "admin" | User's role |
| balance | Number | No | No | 10000 | N/A | User's balance |

3. Complete the `server.js` all the instructions are given in comments.

practiceProblems.title: Registration for user
practiceProblems.description:
Moving further, now we are going to make our authentication routes.

To do this we have created a routes folder in which all the routes would be stored. We have already given you the frontend parts of this project so don't worry about it.

### Task:
1. Complete the `authRoutes.js` to complete the register route:
 * If the user email already exist in the db, give response `User already exists`.
 * If the user is new, store the email, name, role and hashed password.
 * Hashed password should have the salt value of 10.
 * After sucessfully registering the user, give response message `Registered successfully`.

2. Complete the server file:
 * Static load the public folder for the frontend files.
 * Use auth from authRoutes.
 * Serve the login.hthml from the public folder for home route `/`.


#### Notes:
Before submitting, keep the website running for testing.

practiceProblems.title: Login for users
practiceProblems.description:
Now we are going to make the login functionality.

For this we are going to use the jwt tokens for authentication. So we just have to update t out `authRoutes` file and make a new file to check the login credentials and authenticate the password.


#### Task:
1. Complete the `authMiddleware.js`:
 * Check if the token is present or not, if not give response `Authorization header missing`.
 * If it is present verify it with the jwt secret key and give response `Invalid or expired token`.

2. Complete the `authRoutes.js`:
 * To start the `/login` route.
 * If users credentials are not valid give response `Invalid credentials`.
 * Use brcrypt to compare the password stored with the users password.
 * If login is successful, generate the jwt token using **userId**, **userName**, **userRole**, **userBalance**, and sign it with the jwt secret key and set it to expire in 1 hour.
 * And if all of these things are working and the user is logged in give response `Login successful`.
 * Otherwise give `Server error`.

#### Note:
Before submitting, keep the website running for testing.

practiceProblems.title: Money transfer functionality
practiceProblems.description:
In this last problem we are going to handle the Transaction between the users.

For this we have to setup, another mongodb table for transactions, and api to handle those transactions:
| Field | Type | Description | Required | Default | Ref |
|--------------|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------|----------|-------------|--------|
| senderId | ObjectId | ID of the user sending the money | Yes | — | User |
| recipientId | ObjectId | ID of the user receiving the money | Yes | — | User |
| amount | Number | Amount of money transferred | Yes | — | — |
| createdAt | Date | Timestamp of transaction creation | No | `Date.now` | — |

### Task:
1. Complete the `Transaction.js` according to the above given table.
2. Complete the transactions APIs in the `paymentRoute.js` to handle:
 * Find all users who are "customers" but exclude the current user and only send back their name and ID.
 * In `/transfer` API route, complete the task given in the form comments.
 * Complete the `/transaction` API route to show all the transactions of the users.



#### Note:
Before submitting, keep the website running for tests.

practiceProblems.title: Profile picture upload
practiceProblems.description:
Your project is done, but wait the users want to upload their profile pictures, so the team wants to build a new functionality to upload the user images while registering.

To do this we just have to make some change in our files.

#### Task:
1. Complete the `User.js` to store the path of the image for user.

2. We have made a new middleware to handle the upload of the image `uploadMiddleware.js` 

3. Handle the uploads folder which is working as our local storage for the images. Make changes in the `server.js` to server the uploads folder.


### Notes: 
There are more changes to handle this but we have given you those changes in `authMiddleware.js` you can see the changes done there.

To submit the file, first click on run and then submit the problem.
